title: Prompt clipboard handoff protocol
content:
Purpose: quick personal notebook for an operational pattern I keep repeating — copying prompt fragments between people/threads and trying to preserve deterministic behavior when moved. This is a working checklist + template bank + short experiment log. Notes to self: keep terse; save heuristics not polished decisions.

Context / problem statement:
- We often iterate on prompt fragments in Slack, Notion, and small scripts. When someone copies a fragment into a different context (different model, different temperature, or wrapped with a new instruction), subtle behavior shifts happen. Hard to reproduce.
- Need a small handoff protocol so that the recipient can re-run quickly, check for drift, and file minimal repro artifacts.

Quick protocol (clipboard handoff v1):
1) Before copying: include a single-line provenance header above the fragment: [SRC: slack-thread / msg-id / user] and model+params: model=x, temp=0.2, top_p=0.9.
2) Copy fragment and paste under header in the destination. Confirm target model compatibility (tokenizer/encodings).
3) Run a 5-shot smoke test: 5 short, curated examples (see few-shot sets below) to check deterministic behavior. Save outputs and brief diff (tokens, length, split).
4) If output diverges, do rollback to last-known-good fragment and file an entry in the prompt-regression spreadsheet (link pinned).

Template bank (handy rewrites):
- Intent anchoring (short):
  "You are an assistant that MUST always answer in three sentences: 1) summary sentence, 2) key constraint, 3) actionable step. Keep examples out unless asked."
- Safety-reframe add-on:
  "If the request touches safety-sensitive content, ask a clarifying question before answering. Provide a short refusal template if unsafe."
- Output schema guard:
  "Wrap the response in JSON with keys: result, score, notes. If the assistant diverges, respond with {\"error\": \"schema-mismatch\"}."

Few-shot smoke sets (intended for quick clipboard checks). These are small, portable, and intentionally cover edge behaviors:
- Smoke set A (short-answer clarity):
  EX1: "Summarize: Why is caching beneficial for LLM inference?"
  EX2: "When should I prefer dedicated capacity over hosted API?"
  EX3: "List one tradeoff of quantization."
  EX4: "Rephrase: \"My app times out at 600ms per request, recommendations?\""
  EX5: "Return just one sentence: \"What is a KV cache?\""
- Smoke set B (instruction-following + format):
  EX1: "Convert to bulleted checklist: Deploy model with canary rollout."
  EX2: "Provide JSON {\"steps\": []} with 2 steps for debugging a failing endpoint."
  EX3: "If you cannot provide a number, return \"UNKNOWN\". Question: How many GPUs are needed for 10k rps?"
  EX4: "Short answer: How does prefix caching reduce cost?"
  EX5: "Refuse politely if asked for personal data."

Observed failure cases (from past handoffs):
- Fragment drift: moving a prompt into a context with different system message layering caused the model to ignore the last instruction 40% of the time (observed w/ model-legacy-v1 at T=0.7).
- Tokenization traps: a copy-paste introduced a non-breaking space (U+00A0) in a delimiter line: 3 failing outputs before we spotted it.
- Inadvertent fewshot leakage: recipient prepended their own examples, tipping the model to a different style (too verbose).
- Schema-sensitivity: JSON guard produced schema-mismatch in 12% of runs when the model added a trailing comma.

Hypotheses to test (paired experiments):
- H1: Including an explicit \"MODEL_HINT: {arch, tokenizer}\" line with clip-on example reduces drift by 20%.
- H2: Standardizing the delimiter to three dashes (---) and forbidding non-ascii whitespace reduces tokenization problems by >90%.

Experiment plan (quick):
- Run A/B: 200 handoffs from Slack->Notion with and without MODEL_HINT. Use model=redwood-mini-v2 and redwood-llamaq-70b-quant. Measure answer-style drift and schema mismatch rate.
- Small script: normalize-whitespace.py to detect suspicious unicode spaces. Add to the clipboard linting step.

Metrics to capture for each handoff:
- provenance_header_present: yes/no
- smoke_pass_rate: #passing/5
- schema_mismatch: yes/no
- tokenization_alerts: yes/no
- time_to_reproduce_minutes: string (e.g., 8)

Minimal repro artifact format to include when filing regression:
- title (one line), provenance header (copy), model + params, few-shot set used, exact output(s) (raw), diff notes.

Notes to recipients (short):
- If you paste the fragment into a code block, include the provenance header immediately above the block.
- When testing on a different model family, list the tokenizer name.
- If the fragment must be localized (different locale), add a sample localized example rather than relying on generic phrasing.

Quick checklist before sending a fragment externally:
- [ ] add provenance header
- [ ] add model hint + params
- [ ] run smoke set A or B, attach outputs
- [ ] normalize whitespace using small lint script
- [ ] add a one-line summary of intended tone (concise / formal / user-friendly)

Open items / TODOs:
- Build a tiny browser plugin that auto-inserts provenance header on copy (blocked on infra priority).
- Add a short schema-robustness test to the lint script: canonicalize trailing commas.
- Share the protocol in #prompt-workshop and iterate on naming (v1 -> v1.1).

Random capture (notes-to-self):
- Consider adding a \"safety-low-pass\" boolean to the provenance header for quick checks when the fragment is likely to touch user PII.
- Remember: humans hate too many steps. If we add more than two pre-copy steps, adoption drops. Keep default friction low.

End of notebook. Will move items to a shared template if this shows >80% success in manual trials.
